page: Hetzner Cloud cpx22 is an entry-level virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 shared vCPUs consisting of 2 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled as an 80 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance operates under a QEMU hypervisor without any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core CPU performance under stress-ng is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 3059.18, while Geekbench single-core and text processing scores sit in the average tier. However, multi-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% across stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average at 70.65 GB/sec read and 57.5 GB/sec write, but small-block cached read bandwidth and overall Passmark memory scores are weak.

Given its shared CPU allocation and lower multi-core performance, the cpx22 is positioned as a highly cost-efficient option for workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU resources. It exhibits poor static web serving throughput of 2.41 GB/sec and weak database operation metrics, making it less suitable for high-traffic production databases. However, it handles light single-threaded tasks, basic text processing, and small-scale LLM inference acceptably. It is best suited for budget-conscious development environments, lightweight background workers, and low-traffic utility applications.
